source: arXiv:1610.00278v1, equation (6) and Appendix C, native scalar Dirichlet domain and base; dependencies of source Theorem 2.1(ii) and main Theorems 1.4 and 5.1
status: Full classical zero-trace H1 domain exhausted; full dual H-minus-one base, native weak pencil, boundary defect and partial operator constructed. Characteristic equivalence, native resolvent and algebraic multiplicity matching remain open.
results: The unit-period H1 endpoint trace is a continuous linear functional. Its closed kernel is a complete zero-trace H1 domain; every represented function is absolutely continuous on [0,1], has square-integrable derivative and vanishes at BOTH endpoints.

Every classical interval H1 function with zero endpoint values has EXACTLY ONE zero-trace coefficient representative agreeing at EVERY point of the closed interval. The proof assumes no periodicity of the input or its derivative and uses the verified signed classical interval extension and even-frequency Sobolev sampling. Thus the native domain construction exhausts the full interval domain.

The Dirichlet base is the FULL complex continuous dual of this zero-trace H1 space. Restriction from the entire unit-period H1 dual is surjective, with an explicit bounded extension furnished by removing the endpoint trace. The kernel of restriction consists EXACTLY of multiples of endpoint evaluation.

The independent Dirichlet weak operator and spectral pencil are constructed from the unchanged original distributional Hill expression using all zero-trace H1 tests. The unit-period function insertion uses original even frequencies and preserves the original normalized action. Source interpretation on [0,1] uses physically period-one potentials; an arbitrary ambient period-two potential merely defines the induced form.

The native H1-to-H-minus-one domain inclusion is injective and has strictly positive L2 quadratic energy on every nonzero domain vector. Physical conjugation preserves the zero-trace domain and agrees with native distributional conjugation. Both inclusion and singular weak operator retain the original bilinear Green identities.

A native Dirichlet eigen-equation holds IFF the full unit-period residual is precisely a multiple of endpoint evaluation. At EVERY original even frequency its residual coefficient equals the CENTRAL residual coefficient. This retains the boundary defect and does NOT impose equal endpoint values on a quasi-derivative.
Every nontrivial native weak Dirichlet eigenvector for a real original singular potential has REAL eigenvalue, independently of the constructed characteristic or any supplied spectral labels.

The actual partial linear operator acts on the FULL Dirichlet H-minus-one base, with domain exactly the image of the complete zero-trace H1 space. Its entire graph is identified with the weak operator graph, and its nonzero eigenvectors are equivalent to nonzero kernels of the independently defined native pencil.
essential_remaining: Prove the native weak Dirichlet eigen-equation is equivalent to the independently constructed absolutely continuous quasi-derivative boundary problem for arbitrary complex original H-minus-one source potentials. In the reverse regularity argument retain the now-proved endpoint-evaluation defect rather than forcing the quasi-derivative to be periodic.

Prove closedness and resolvent properties for the actual Dirichlet partial operator, and identify its full spectrum and ALGEBRAIC multiplicities with the normalized entire Dirichlet characteristic. The full zero-trace domain and H-minus-one base are now independently constructed and the classical domain exhaustion is proved; characteristic/operator matching is still open.

Complete global COMPLEX Dirichlet central labels and the full COMPLEX general-weight midpoint estimate/local boundedness in source Theorem 2.1(ii). Full REAL characteristic labels, all analytic multiplicities and weighted midpoint membership remain proved, but uniform real norm-ball estimates are not inferred from finite modification.

Complete the remaining low periodic simplicity/interlacing and periodic/antiperiodic boundary parity, general complex-ratio Lemma 2.20, original KdV Birkhoff maps and actual H-minus-one approximation flow. Main Theorems 1.1,1.3,1.4,5.1,5.9 remain UNPROVED.
native_domain: H_dir^1([0,1], C), represented by unit-period H1 coefficients with zero endpoint trace
native_base: Full continuous complex dual of H_dir^1([0,1], C)
qualifications: Unit-period source potentials are required for the source interval interpretation of the normalized original period-two form; the definition for an arbitrary ambient period-two potential is its induced zero-trace form.
The source sesquilinear weak action is recovered by the proved physical conjugation of the test vector. The underlying full complex linear dual is used as the base.
No quasi-derivative endpoint equality or extra scalar derivative trace is imposed. Native eigen-equations allow the exact endpoint-evaluation residual.

The entire classical scalar H1 interval domain is represented, but no assertion of closedness, dense resolvent range, compact resolvent, complete native spectrum or native algebraic multiplicity matching is made in this milestone.
All five main theorems remain unproved.
